quarterly_data.signal: Alphabet Q2 2026 results (CFO Anat Ashkenazi): 'our 12th consecutive quarter of double-digit revenue growth'. Consolidated revenues were $119.8 billion, up 24%, or 23% in constant currency. Total cost of revenues was $45.9 billion, up 18%; TAC ('Tech' in the transcript) was $16.2 billion, up 10%; other cost of revenues was $29.8 billion, up 22%, driven by increases in depreciation, inventory costs primarily from the sales of TPU systems to customers, and content acquisition costs, largely for YouTube. Total operating expenses were up 27% to $33.1 billion; R&D expenses increased 32%, driven by compensation from investments in AI talent as well as depreciation; sales and marketing rose 18% on investments to support the Gemini app and Search. Operating income increased 30% to $40.8 billion and operating margin was 34%. Other income and expenses was $98 billion, primarily unrealized gains in the equity securities portfolio. Operating cash flow was $185.7 billion and free cash flow $53.3 billion for the trailing 12 months.
quarterly_data.figure: revenues $119.8 billion (up 24%, 23% in constant currency); operating income $40.8 billion (up 30%), operating margin 34%; trailing-12-month operating cash flow $185.7 billion, free cash flow $53.3 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Segment results (CFO Anat Ashkenazi): Google Services revenues increased 15% to $94.5 billion, reflecting strong growth in Search and subscriptions; total advertising revenues were up 14% with growth across all major verticals, and strong ad growth related to the World Cup, particularly in YouTube ads. Google Search & other advertising revenues increased 17% to $63.3 billion, with retail and finance driving the largest contributions; YouTube advertising revenues increased 13% to $11.1 billion, driven by direct response and brand, with strength in the living room; Network advertising revenues of $7.3 billion were down 1%; subscriptions, platforms and devices revenues increased 15% to $12.9 billion on YouTube subscriptions (particularly YouTube Music and Premium) and Google One, driven by demand for AI plans. Google Services operating income increased 20% to $39.5 billion, an operating margin of 41.8%. Alphabet-level activities had an operating loss of $5.8 billion, driven by shared AI R&D expenses.
quarterly_data.figure: Google Services $94.5 billion (up 15%), operating income $39.5 billion, margin 41.8%; Search & other $63.3 billion (up 17%); YouTube ads $11.1 billion (up 13%); Network $7.3 billion (down 1%); subscriptions, platforms and devices $12.9 billion (up 15%)

quarterly_data.signal: Outlook for the second half of 2026 (CFO Anat Ashkenazi): at current spot rates Alphabet expects a slight FX headwind to consolidated revenue in Q3, compared to a 1 percentage point FX tailwind in Q2, seen primarily in Search and YouTube ads; in Q3 Google will begin lapping an acceleration in Search performance that began in the third quarter last year. In Google Cloud 'we are seeing significant demand for products and services, which we expect to drive strong growth'. The significant increase in technical-infrastructure investment will continue to pressure the P&L through higher depreciation expense and related data-center operations costs such as energy; hiring continues in key areas such as AI and Cloud, with marketing investment behind AI products; free cash flow is expected to remain under pressure from technical-infrastructure investment. The integration of Wiz creates some headwind to Cloud operating margins in the near term in 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: slight Q3 FX headwind vs a 1 percentage point FX tailwind in Q2; free cash flow to remain under pressure

quarterly_data.signal: Compute supply (CFO Anat Ashkenazi, Q&A): 'We're still in a supply constraint environment'; demand is very strong 'both from external cloud customers as well as across the business', and 'while we have increased our capacity quite significantly over the past three years, the demand still outpaces that investment. We are, just like the rest of the industry, working in a supply-constrained environment.' The full-stack approach lets Google drive operational and technological efficiencies in its technical infrastructure so it can deliver more compute. CEO Sundar Pichai: 'the industry has constraints, too'; he described the third-party bridge capacity as taking an upfront six-month deal to serve a customer in a multi-year opportunity where margins and returns are very attractive over that horizon.

TPU system sales (Q&A): CEO Sundar Pichai said 'A lot of our cloud serving is done on TPUs, and we are also seeing strong demand for TPUs as standalone systems from other customers'; for Cloud customers Google uses both TPUs and GPUs mainly to serve its models (Vertex AI, Gemini Enterprise, agentic workloads). Asked about a merchant-silicon business he said 'I don't want to project out too far into the future there' and that Google will scale up based on the opportunities and demand it sees. CFO Anat Ashkenazi: Google builds inventory ahead to sell the systems, which shows in cash from operations, and generally starts recognizing revenue once deliveries start; this quarter was a small amount of the total agreement. Google does not break out TPU margins, but 'there are benefits from designing and manufacturing our own chips', and TPU system sales are 'an expansion of our total addressable market', providing solutions to customers that need those systems in their data centers.

Cloud backlog composition (CFO Anat Ashkenazi): the increase in Google Cloud's backlog to $514 billion 'was driven by strong demand for our enterprise AI offerings'; 'The majority of the backlog is related to typical GCP contracts from a broad mix of customers'. In Q&A: 'The vast majority of the $514 billion of cloud backlog is the GCP agreements, but the TPU system sales are reflected in that backlog', entering it when the agreements are signed. CEO Sundar Pichai cited strong demand indicators for 2027 capacity planning, 'including long-term deals, the existing deals which we have, which are renewing with exceptional demand'.
quarterly_data.figure: Google Cloud backlog $514 billion, vast majority GCP agreements, TPU system sale agreements included

capex.growth: increased by more than $50 billion sequentially

quarterly_data.signal: Capex and returns (Q&A): CFO Anat Ashkenazi - 'Our goal is to invest as long as we see an attractive return on that investment'; Google takes a multi-year view of capacity needs while focusing on next year and the near term and 'building aggressively to meet those demands'. CEO Sundar Pichai - Google works off 'a discipline ROIC framework', and rising input costs are reflected 'in our ability to price our solutions'; for 2027 compute capacity investments, 'if anything, the dynamics look healthier than where we were about a year ago, that's what gives us the confidence to undertake those investments'; on the GenAI opportunity, 'over the past year, we've gotten more bullish on the opportunities ahead'. Full-year 2026 CapEx guidance is $195 billion-$205 billion; CapEx is expected to increase significantly in 2027, with more details at a later date.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 CapEx guidance $195 billion-$205 billion; 2027 CapEx expected to increase significantly

quarterly_data.signal: Google Cloud adoption (CEO Sundar Pichai): nearly 90% of the Fortune 100 use Gemini Enterprise; transactions on Google Cloud Marketplace grew over seven times year over year; the Agent Development Kit reached nearly 70 million total downloads in Q2; the momentum is driving growth in paid token usage. Security: 90% of the Fortune 100 are Google Cloud security users, nearly 90% of Wiz customers use AI-powered security features, and the number of AI workloads scanned and protected by the security platform rose more than 45% quarter over quarter; the new Google AI Threat Defense brings the new cyber model and CodeMender to customers.
quarterly_data.figure: nearly 90% of the Fortune 100 use Gemini Enterprise; Marketplace transactions over seven times year over year; Agent Development Kit nearly 70 million downloads; AI workloads protected up more than 45% quarter over quarter

quarterly_data.signal: Search and ads (Sundar Pichai / Philipp Schindler): AI Overviews and AI Mode are now one Search experience; just like AI Overviews, AI Mode is driving an incremental increase in Search queries overall, Search usage hit an all-time high during the World Cup, and AI features in Search send billions of clicks to websites every week. Gemini improves query understanding for ads: shopping ads drove a 20% improvement in showing highly relevant ads; AI Max is out of beta with 500,000 advertisers, and advertisers adopting AI Max or Performance Max see an average of 15% more conversions or value on Search at a similar ROAS; AI Max 'continues to unlock' 'billions of net new searches that weren't really monetizable before'; over half of SMB customers globally use AI to create or optimize their creatives. Monetization on queries that show AI Overviews remains encouraging even as AI Overviews expand to more commercial queries; AI Mode is testing new ad formats (contextual site links in text ads, Direct Offers, sponsored links in Highlighted Answers). Merchants are adopting the open-source Universal Commerce Protocol for agentic commerce, with Target and Steve Madden live, and Universal Cart lets shoppers buy from different retailers in a single checkout.
quarterly_data.figure: shopping ads 20% improvement in showing highly relevant ads; AI Max adopted by 500,000 advertisers; 15% more conversions or value at similar ROAS

quarterly_data.signal: YouTube (Sundar Pichai / Philipp Schindler): over 1.7 billion unique viewers watched World Cup-related videos on YouTube during the FIFA World Cup 2026 and over 550 million watched them on their televisions, making it the most viewed World Cup in YouTube history; more than 140 million users engaged with Ask YouTube on the Watch page in June 2026. The YouTube subscription business is growing faster than ads, particularly driven by YouTube Music and Premium; Buy with Google Pay lets CTV viewers complete purchases directly on their TV. Growth drivers cited: brand opportunities on CTVs in the living room, exclusive creator shows, Demand Gen and Shorts for small and medium advertisers, and shoppable ad formats in the living room.
quarterly_data.figure: over 1.7 billion unique World Cup viewers (over 550 million on TVs); more than 140 million Ask YouTube users in June 2026

quarterly_data.figure: Other Bets revenues $382 million, operating loss $1.8 billion; Wing more than one million home deliveries
